name: lecture-slides-v1
description: Questions over five PDF lecture decks (regression modelling and database design). Gold labels are the page numbers that contain the answer. Splits: heldout = written for this evaluation; dev = questions asked during development, which the retrieval rules were tuned on; unanswerable = not covered by any document.

documents.topic: Regression: diagnostics and goodness of fit

questions.question: What three components define every generalized linear model?
questions.reference: A probability distribution for the response from the exponential family; a linear combination of the explanatory variables; and a link function that relates the expected value of the response to that linear combination.

questions.question: In the catheter study, how many patients were measured and which variables were recorded?
questions.reference: 12 young patients; their height (inches), weight (pounds) and catheter length (cm) were recorded.

questions.question: What were the null and residual deviances for the Gaussian GLM fitted to the catheter data?
questions.reference: Null deviance 735.67 on 11 degrees of freedom; residual deviance 128.48 on 9 degrees of freedom.

questions.question: 导管长度的例子中，拟合出来的回归方程是什么？
questions.reference: Fitted mean catheter length = 20.38 + 0.21 x height + 0.19 x weight (coefficients 20.3758, 0.2107, 0.1911); estimated error variance about 14.27.

questions.question: How should the coefficient for height be interpreted in the catheter model?
questions.reference: It is the slope of the fitted plane when height varies and weight is held constant, i.e. the change in fitted catheter length per unit of height at a fixed weight.

questions.question: What is the 95% confidence interval for the height coefficient in the catheter model, and is height significant?
questions.reference: The 95% confidence interval is (-0.466, 0.888). Height is not significant: its p-value (0.557) is above 0.05, so there is no evidence to reject beta_ht = 0.

questions.question: For a child 44 inches tall weighing 35 pounds, what catheter length does the model predict and what is the 95% prediction interval?
questions.reference: Predicted length about 36.34 cm; 95% prediction interval about (26.61, 46.06). (The 95% confidence interval for the mean is (31.69, 40.98).)

questions.question: 为什么大多数GLM的最大似然估计没有显式解？用什么算法求解？
questions.reference: For most GLMs, including logistic and Poisson regression, the equations from setting the derivatives of the log-likelihood to zero are not linear, so there is no explicit solution. They are solved numerically with iteratively re-weighted least squares (IRLS), which glm() in R uses. For ordinary regression the ML estimate equals least squares, (X^T X)^-1 X^T Y.

questions.question: What are the steps of the usual approach to maximum likelihood estimation for GLMs?
questions.reference: (i) Write down the log-likelihood (maximising it gives the same estimates and is easier); (ii) take partial derivatives with respect to the parameters; (iii) set them to zero and solve.

questions.question: In the CHD example, what is the estimated coefficient for age in the logistic regression, and what is the fitted model?
questions.reference: The age coefficient is about 0.110 (intercept about -5.278). Fitted model: p = exp(-5.28 + 0.11 x age) / (1 + exp(-5.28 + 0.11 x age)).

questions.question: Why is the first confidence interval for the probability of CHD at age 25 described as rough, and what better alternative is used?
questions.reference: The normal-approximation interval on the probability scale, 0.0744 +/- 1.96 x 0.0384, is (-0.0009, 0.150), which contains negative values. The better approach builds the interval on the linear predictor (logit) scale, (-3.613, -1.428), and transforms the end points with the logistic function, giving about (0.026, 0.193).

questions.question: probit 回归和 logistic 回归有什么区别？什么时候结果会差别比较大？
questions.reference: Probit regression uses the standard normal CDF as the link (p = Phi(X beta)) instead of the logit link. Both curves are S-shaped and roughly linear in the middle, so the fitted models are very similar; they differ mainly when estimated probabilities are near 0 or 1.

questions.question: In the horseshoe crab example, what is the response variable and which link function is used?
questions.reference: The response is the number of satellite males (a count), assumed Poisson with mean mu; the link is the log link: log(mu) = beta0 + beta1 x weight + colour indicator terms.

questions.question: 在螃蟹（horseshoe crab）的泊松回归中，weight 的系数估计是多少？是否显著？
questions.reference: About 0.546 (standard error 0.068, z = 8.02, p about 1e-15), so weight is highly significant.

questions.question: What does the covariance matrix of Y reduce to when the observations are independent with common variance sigma squared?
questions.reference: sigma^2 I_n: a diagonal matrix with sigma^2 on the diagonal, where I_n is the n x n identity matrix.

questions.question: logit 函数和 expit 函数分别是什么？它们是什么关系？
questions.reference: logit(p) = log(p / (1 - p)) for p in (0, 1), the log-odds; expit(x) = exp(x) / (1 + exp(x)) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x)). They are inverses of each other.

questions.question: Which distributions does the generalized linear model family include besides the normal, binomial and Poisson?
questions.reference: Gamma and inverse-Gaussian (continuous responses on [0, infinity)), Beta (continuous responses on [0, 1]) and negative binomial (counts with Var(Y) >= E(Y)), among others.

questions.question: 统计推断在什么情况下可能产生误导？
questions.reference: Inference depends on assumptions about the data; if they are violated it may be misleading. It is also only valid for the population that produced the data. Assumptions are seldom exactly right, but inference is useful if they are close enough.

questions.question: What is a sampling distribution, and how do we imagine new samples for regression models?
questions.reference: The distribution of estimates obtained by fitting the model to a large number of samples; since collecting many samples is impractical, theory is used to derive it when the assumptions hold. For regression we imagine new data where the explanatory values stay the same but the response changes.

questions.question: What topics does the course overview list under regularization and flexible regression?
questions.reference: Ridge and LASSO, splines, and tree-based methods.

questions.question: What is the difference between an error and a residual?
questions.reference: An error is the difference between an observation and the mean from the true model, which cannot be known because the true coefficients are unknown. A residual is the observed value minus the fitted value from the estimated model, i.e. an estimate of the error.

questions.question: Cook 距离衡量的是什么？值大说明什么？
questions.reference: It measures the overall change in the estimated coefficients when the i-th observation is removed (relative to the local curvature of the likelihood). A large value means the observation has a large effect on the model fit and the conclusions.

questions.question: What does the diagonal of the hat matrix measure, and what range do its values take?
questions.reference: The diagonal element h_ii measures the leverage of observation i, i.e. how far its predictors are from the centre of the predictor space; 0 <= h_ii <= 1 and larger means higher leverage. H = X (X^T X)^-1 X^T maps Y to the fitted values.

questions.question: Which data problems and which model problems are diagnostics meant to detect?
questions.reference: Data issues: outliers, high-leverage points, influential points and multicollinearity. Model issues: the assumptions (linearity, normality, independent errors with constant variance) not being adequately satisfied.

questions.question: 什么是饱和模型（saturated model）？
questions.reference: The model with the best possible fit: for each distinct covariate pattern the fitted value maximises the likelihood (e.g. the fitted proportion equals the observed proportion; for ordinary regression mu_i = y_i and RSS = 0). The deviance compares a model with it.

questions.question: What is the formula for the F-statistic in the added-variable test?
questions.reference: f0 = [(RSS_sub - RSS_full) / (k_full - k_sub)] / [RSS_full / (n - k_full - 1)], compared with an F distribution on (k_full - k_sub, n - k_full - 1) degrees of freedom; p-value = Pr(F >= f0).

questions.question: For the catheter regression, what were the R-squared and the overall F-test result?
questions.reference: Multiple R-squared 0.8254 (adjusted 0.7865); F = 21.27 on 2 and 9 degrees of freedom, p = 0.00039, so the regression explains significantly more than the intercept-only model.

questions.question: 在导管数据中，已经有身高的模型里再加入体重，F 检验的结论是什么？
questions.reference: anova(ht.lm, full.lm) gives F = 1.46 with p = 0.258, so weight adds no significant information once height is in the model.

questions.question: When is the chi-squared approximation for the Pearson goodness-of-fit statistic reliable?
questions.reference: When most r_i >= 5 and n_i - r_i >= 5, roughly large group sizes with probabilities not close to 0 or 1. The statistic then has approximately a chi-squared distribution with n - k - 1 degrees of freedom.

questions.question: What did the goodness-of-fit test conclude for the logit and probit models of the CHD data?
questions.reference: Deviances 34.976 (logit) and 35.109 (probit) on 41 degrees of freedom, p-values 0.734 and 0.729: insufficient evidence of a difference from the saturated model, i.e. no evidence of lack of fit.

questions.question: 似然比检验的统计量怎么计算？服从什么分布？
questions.reference: d0 = Dev_sub - Dev_full, the change in deviance between the submodel and the full model. Under the null hypothesis that the extra regressors are not needed (and for large samples) it is approximately chi-squared with degrees of freedom equal to the number of additional regressors.

questions.question: In the CHD example, what is the likelihood ratio test statistic for adding age, and its p-value?
questions.reference: d0 = 63.958 - 34.976 = 28.982 on 1 degree of freedom; p-value about 7.3e-08.

questions.question: Why does the p-value for colour change so much depending on whether it enters the crab model before or after weight?
questions.reference: anova() tests terms sequentially, and weight and colour are correlated (lighter crabs tend to be larger), so their effects overlap. Colour entered first has p = 3e-05, but after weight its p-value is only 0.028.

questions.question: 准泊松（quasipoisson）模型估计出来的离散参数是多少？说明什么？
questions.reference: About 3.18: the variance is estimated to be 3.18 times that of the Poisson model, i.e. the data are overdispersed.

questions.question: What are two plausible causes of overdispersion in the crab data?
questions.reference: A missing explanatory variable, and the satellites not acting independently.

questions.question: What are the mean and variance of the negative binomial distribution, and what happens as theta goes to infinity?
questions.reference: E(X) = mu and Var(X) = mu + mu^2 / theta. The variance always exceeds the mean but approaches it as theta grows, and as theta goes to infinity the negative binomial becomes the Poisson distribution.

questions.question: 为什么不能直接用 glm() 拟合负二项回归？R 里用什么函数？
questions.reference: The negative binomial is in the exponential family only when theta is fixed, and theta usually has to be estimated, so glm() cannot be used. Use glm.nb() from the MASS package, which fixes theta, fits with the glm algorithm, updates theta and repeats until convergence.

questions.question: What are the trade-offs between using a quasi-likelihood model and a full distributional model such as the negative binomial?
questions.reference: Quasi-models handle both under- and overdispersion through the dispersion parameter, but likelihood theory no longer holds, so deviance and goodness-of-fit tests cannot be used. Distributional models give full likelihood-based methods but restrict the dispersion structure: negative binomial and beta-binomial cannot model underdispersion, and Conway-Maxwell-Poisson allows both but its probability mass function cannot be computed exactly.

questions.question: What is an offset in a Poisson regression, and why would you use one?
questions.reference: An offset is a regressor whose coefficient is fixed at 1, such as log(pop / 100000). It is used when counts were taken over different population sizes or time periods, so that the other regressors model a rate (e.g. per 100,000) rather than a raw count.

questions.question: 儿童癌症例子里，城市居民的癌症死亡率是农村的多少倍？
questions.reference: About 1.44 times, i.e. exp(0.3677).

questions.question: Which interaction term in the childhood cancer model is clearly significant?
questions.reference: Cytology:Age (p about 0.003); the other interaction terms are not clearly significant.

questions.question: What are the three levels of the three-schema architecture and what does each describe?
questions.reference: The internal level describes physical storage structures and access paths; the conceptual level describes the structure and constraints of the whole database for a community of users; the external level describes the various user views.

questions.question: 逻辑数据独立性和物理数据独立性有什么区别？
questions.reference: Logical data independence: the conceptual schema can change without changing the external schemas and application programs. Physical data independence: the internal schema can change (e.g. reorganised files, new indexes) without changing the conceptual schema.

questions.question: How does a database schema differ from a database state?
questions.reference: The schema is the description of the database (structure, data types, constraints) and changes very infrequently. The state, also called instance or snapshot, is the actual data at a particular moment and changes every time the database is updated.

questions.question: What is the difference between procedural and non-procedural DML?
questions.reference: Non-procedural (high-level, declarative) DML such as SQL is set-oriented and specifies what data to retrieve rather than how. Procedural (low-level) DML retrieves one record at a time, needs looping and positioning pointers, and must be embedded in a programming language.

questions.question: 三层客户端-服务器架构的中间层负责什么？为什么能提高安全性？
questions.reference: The middle tier (application or web server) holds the web connectivity software and business logic and passes partially processed data between the database server and the clients. Security improves because the database server is only accessible through the middle tier; clients cannot access it directly.

questions.question: What are the main categories of data models?
questions.reference: Conceptual (high-level, entity-based) models, physical (low-level) models, implementation or representational models such as the relational model, and self-describing models such as XML and key-value.

questions.question: Give examples of programming-language interfaces to a DBMS.
questions.reference: Embedded SQL (for C/C++) and SQLJ (for Java); procedure-call APIs such as JDBC and ODBC; database programming languages such as Oracle PL/SQL; and scripting languages such as PHP and Python.

questions.question: DBMS 按数据模型可以分成哪些类型？
questions.reference: Legacy: network and hierarchical. Currently used: relational, object-oriented and object-relational. Recent: key-value and NoSQL systems (document, column, graph, key-value) and native XML DBMSs.

questions.question: What kinds of tasks do database system utilities perform?
questions.reference: Loading data from files (with conversion tools), periodic backup, reorganising database file structures, performance monitoring, report generation, and other functions such as sorting, user monitoring and data compression.

questions.question: What is the role of DDL, SDL and VDL?
questions.reference: DDL is used by the DBA and designers to specify the conceptual schema (and in many DBMSs also internal and external schemas). Where they are separate, SDL (storage definition language) defines the internal schema and VDL (view definition language) defines the external schemas or views.

questions.question: What is the difference between a composite attribute and a multi-valued attribute?
questions.reference: A composite attribute is made of several components, e.g. Address(Apt#, House#, Street, City, ...) or Name(FirstName, MiddleName, LastName). A multi-valued attribute can have several values for one entity, e.g. the colours of a car or a student's previous degrees, written in braces.

questions.question: 什么是派生属性？举个例子。
questions.reference: An attribute whose value is derived from another attribute and may change over time, e.g. a person's age derived from the date of birth. It is drawn as a dashed oval.

questions.question: Can an entity type have more than one key? Give the example used in the slides.
questions.reference: Yes. The CAR entity type has two keys: VehicleIdentificationNumber (VIN) and VehicleTagNumber (Number, State), which is a composite key. Each key is underlined.

questions.question: How are entity types, attributes, key attributes and multivalued attributes drawn in an ER diagram?
questions.reference: Entity types are rectangles, attributes are ovals connected to their entity type, key attributes are underlined, and multivalued attributes are double ovals; components of a composite attribute connect to its oval.

questions.question: COMPANY 数据库中，每个部门需要记录哪些信息？
questions.reference: Each department has a name, a number and an employee who manages it, with the manager's start date tracked; a department may have several locations, and it controls a number of projects.

questions.question: Which six relationship types are identified for the COMPANY database?
questions.reference: WORKS_FOR, MANAGES, CONTROLS, WORKS_ON, SUPERVISION and DEPENDENTS_OF, all binary.

questions.question: What is the cardinality ratio of WORKS_ON between EMPLOYEE and PROJECT, compared with WORKS_FOR?
questions.reference: WORKS_ON between EMPLOYEE and PROJECT is M:N, while WORKS_FOR between EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT is N:1.

questions.question: 关系类型（relationship type）的度（degree）指的是什么？
questions.reference: The number of participating entity types. MANAGES and WORKS_ON have degree 2 (binary); degree 3 is ternary and degree n is n-ary.

questions.question: What is the difference between a relationship type and a relationship set?
questions.reference: A relationship type is the schema description: the relationship name, the participating entity types and constraints. A relationship set is the current set of relationship instances in the database, i.e. the current state of the relationship type.

questions.question: What is an entity set?
questions.reference: The collection of entities of a given entity type stored in the database (also called entity collection), i.e. the current state of the entities of that type.

questions.question: How is an attribute defined mathematically in the ER model?
questions.reference: As a function A : E -> P(V) from the entity type E to the power set of its value set V, which covers simple and multivalued attributes; A(e) is the value of attribute A for entity e.

questions.question: What is a weak entity type, and how are its entities identified?
questions.reference: An entity type with no key attribute that is identification-dependent on an owner entity type through an identifying relationship. Its entities are identified by a partial key (underlined with a dashed line) together with the related owner entity, e.g. DEPENDENT identified by the dependent's name and the EMPLOYEE via DEPENDENT_OF.

questions.question: 什么是递归关系？举例说明。
questions.reference: A relationship type in which the same entity type participates more than once in distinct roles (self-referencing), e.g. SUPERVISION, where one EMPLOYEE is the supervisor and another EMPLOYEE is the supervisee. Role names are needed in the diagram.

questions.question: In (min, max) notation, what constraints are given for EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT in the MANAGES relationship?
questions.reference: EMPLOYEE participates with (0,1), since an employee manages at most one department; DEPARTMENT participates with (1,1), since each department has exactly one manager.

questions.question: How are total and partial participation shown in an ER diagram?
questions.reference: Total participation (existence dependency) is shown with a double line and partial participation with a single line.

questions.question: 关系上的约束有哪两类？分别规定什么？
questions.reference: The cardinality ratio, which specifies maximum participation (1:1, 1:N or N:1, M:N), and the participation (existence dependency) constraint, which specifies minimum participation: zero for optional, one or more for mandatory.

questions.question: When can an attribute of a relationship type be moved to one of the participating entity types?
questions.reference: In a 1:N relationship the attribute can be moved to the entity type on the N side. Relationship attributes such as HoursPerWeek of WORKS_ON are mostly needed for M:N relationships.

questions.question: Is a ternary relationship equivalent to three binary relationships?
questions.reference: No. In general an n-ary relationship is not equivalent to n binary relationships; three binary relationships can represent different information than one ternary relationship, and both can be included if they convey different meanings.

questions.question: UML 类图是怎么表示实体类型和关系的？
questions.reference: Classes, which are similar to entity types, are boxes with three sections: the class name, the attributes and the operations. Relationships are called associations and are drawn as lines connecting the classes.

questions.question: What are the pros and cons of commercial data modeling tools mentioned in the lecture?
questions.reference: Pros: they document the application requirements and offer an easy, mostly graphical editor. Cons: most lack a proper notation for relationships with attributes, and they mostly show a relational design in diagram form rather than a conceptual ER design.

questions.question: When is a binary relationship redundant with respect to a ternary relationship?
questions.reference: When it can always be derived from the higher-degree relationship, e.g. TAUGHT_DURING can be derived from the ternary relationship OFFERS.

questions.question: What are the uses of regression?
questions.reference: Understanding the data-generating process (interpreting parameters, direction and size of effects, relevant variables, scientific explanation); prediction (minimising predictive risk); and causal inference (E[Y | do X], which needs identification assumptions and confounding control).

questions.question: 什么是GLM？
questions.reference: A generalized linear model: a broad class of regression models (including normal, logistic and Poisson regression) in which the response comes from an exponential-family distribution, a link function of the mean equals a linear combination of the explanatory variables, observations are independent, and the variance is determined by the distribution.

questions.question: 什么是线性回归？
questions.reference: A model for the conditional mean of a response given explanatory variables, E[Y_i | X_i] = beta0 + beta1 X1i + ... + betak Xki, with an intercept and coefficients to estimate; in normal (ordinary) regression Y_i ~ Normal(mu_i, sigma^2) with constant variance.

questions.question: 什么是p value？
questions.reference: The probability, under the null hypothesis, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed, e.g. Pr(F >= f0) for the added-variable F-test or Pr(D >= d0) with D ~ chi-squared for the deviance test. A p-value above 0.05 means no significant evidence against the null hypothesis.

questions.question: Normal regression 的GLM数学公式是什么？
questions.reference: Y_i ~ Normal(mu_i, sigma^2) with mu_i = beta0 + beta1 X1i + ... + betak Xki (identity link); in matrix form Y ~ Normal(mu, sigma^2 I_n) with mu = X beta.

questions.question: Residual是什么？
questions.reference: The observed response minus the fitted value from the estimated model, Y_i - mu_hat_i(X_i), which estimates the unobservable true error. In ordinary regression residuals should be roughly normal with mean 0 and variance sigma^2.

questions.question: Pearson residuals的数学表示是什么？
questions.reference: r_i = (Y_i - mu_hat_i(X_i)) / sqrt(Var(Y_i | X_i)); for binomial data r_i = (Y_i - n_i p_hat_i) / sqrt(n_i p_hat_i (1 - p_hat_i)).

questions.question: deviance是什么模型和什么模型比较？
questions.reference: It compares the fitted model with the saturated (best possible) model: Dev = 2 log L_sat - 2 log L_mod.

questions.question: intercept是什么？
questions.reference: The intercept beta0 is the value of the fitted response when all explanatory variables are 0 (in the catheter model, the fitted length when height and weight are both 0).
